Our Story

Named After A Protector.
Built By One.

Saint Michaels Coffee wasn't reverse engineered from a marketing plan. It's one family, one name, and one life spent serving, in the order it actually happened.

Join the Waitlist

The story of Saint Michaels begins before Michael was born, with his father and the woman who helped raise him.

The Woman Who Raised His Father

Michael’s father, Harold James Englert (Jim), was raised at Saint Joseph’s Villa in Rochester, New York. There, Sister Mary Elaine became not only a mentor, but the closest thing to a mother that place could give a boy. Her care and guidance stayed with him throughout his life.

Her Devotion to Saint Michael

Sister Mary Elaine had a special devotion to Saint Michael the Archangel.

A Name That Carried Her Legacy

Years later, Jim named his firstborn son, Michael James Englert, after Saint Michael the Archangel, honoring Sister Mary Elaine and her devotion to the saint. That son is our founder.

Honoring Harold James Englert

The Man Behind the Man

Jim served as a U.S. Navy Seabee during the Vietnam War. We honor his service to our country and the lasting example he set for his firstborn son.

Jim gave Michael more than his name. He shaped the man he would become. Michael credits his father with his work ethic and everything good he learned along the way.

The Founder

Michael James Englert

U.S. Army veteran and Police Sergeant with more than two decades on the job. Amateur and professional boxer, now a trainer of amateur boxers and founder of Saint Michaels Boxing Club.

Different uniforms, one thread running through all of them: he goes first, and he brings people with him.

A Lifetime Of Service

It all started with boxing. As a boy in Rochester, New York, Michael was heading toward trouble when a police officer helped point him toward a boxing gym. He began boxing at age 11, competing as an amateur before turning professional. He later put his professional boxing career on hold for military service in the United States Army, Special Forces. He also serves his community as a police officer, rising to Sergeant. Today, he trains amateur and pro boxers and gives young people the kind of chance he was given.

Read Michael’s story in The Herald

Saint Michaels Boxing Club

That mentoring turned into something bigger: Saint Michaels Boxing Club, a nonprofit boxing gym serving underprivileged youth. It gives young people discipline, structure, and someone in their corner, the same things Sister Mary Elaine once gave his father.

Visit Saint Michaels Boxing Club

The name passed from a father to his son, then became part of a boxing club built to help others. Saint Michaels Coffee carries that story into its next chapter.

Coffee, The Whole Way Through

Across every one of those worlds, deployments, police shifts, firehouses, boxing gyms, kitchen tables, the same thing kept showing up. Coffee before the mission. Coffee through the long shift. Coffee at the gym. Coffee when people finally sat down together.

And Eventually, Coffee With A Purpose

That's what became Saint Michaels Coffee: a way to carry where he came from and what he's done into something that keeps helping people, one bag at a time.

Protect what matters. Serve others.
Leave things better than you found them.

Coffee With A Purpose

Great Coffee. Greater Purpose.

Saint Michaels Coffee is committed to supporting charitable organizations and causes that serve first responders, veterans, youth, families, and communities in need. We are also building Saint Michaels Foundation to help trusted frontliners put immediate, practical assistance within reach. The Foundation is coming soon.
